a.headline: It's not meant to replace your creativity: Adobe's AI pitch hasn't changed in two years, but the tools have
a.summary: Adobe continues to frame its AI tools as creative assistants rather than replacements, but two years on the actual capabilities have shifted significantly. As a design student, this is a useful reality check on how the industry rhetoric around AI compares to what the tools now actually do in practice.

a.headline: It's official: creatives are using AI daily, but most aren't making extra money from it
a.summary: Envato surveyed over 1,000 creatives and found that daily AI use is now routine across the industry, yet financial gains remain elusive and clients are often kept in the dark. For design students entering the profession, this paints a candid picture of how AI is actually embedded in studio workflows right now.

a.headline: GTA 6 is proof that human creativity is still the most impressive technology we have
a.summary: The release of GTA VI has prompted a wider conversation about the irreplaceable value of human craft, from animating a character opening a door with her hip to building an entire fictional city from real cultural references. For motion and game design students, it is a timely argument for the depth that only sustained human creative labour can produce.

b.headline: Data centers' electricity use is soaring — especially in these states
b.summary: A new analysis reveals that data centres now consume around 2 percent of all US electricity, with some states carrying a far heavier burden as AI infrastructure scales rapidly. The piece puts hard numbers on the energy cost of the AI tools design students use every day, making the abstract environmental argument concrete.

b.headline: Even the good guys of AI are locking in fossil fuels
b.summary: Anthropic, widely regarded as one of the more ethically minded AI companies, has been found to be deepening reliance on fossil fuel energy sources as it scales its infrastructure following a 1.5 trillion dollar valuation. This is essential reading for design students who want to understand the environmental contradictions embedded in the generative tools they use.

b.headline: Datacentre bosses met Australian state premiers and ministers almost 120 times in three years, analysis finds
b.summary: An investigation has found that data centre executives have had extensive and largely opaque access to senior government figures as AI infrastructure expansion accelerates across Australia. It reveals the political lobbying machinery behind decisions about where energy-hungry AI facilities get built and who bears the cost.

c.headline: Dapper Liam and Noel, experimental Björk, and Bowie cuddling himself: Rankin reveals his never-before-seen shots of the stars
c.summary: Renowned photographer Rankin describes his experiments with AI as producing results he found disgusting, and has returned emphatically to analogue photographic practice with a new book of contact sheets. His public rejection of AI aesthetics in favour of the unmediated energy of film is a compelling statement from one of the industry's most prominent image-makers.

c.headline: The Long Way to I Do: A Porsche Love Story, Hand-Painted Frame by Frame
c.summary: Director Em Cooper hand-painted every frame of a film for Porsche, transforming a documentary subject into a moving oil painting through entirely manual means. At a moment when AI-generated animation is proliferating, this project is a deliberate and powerful argument for the expressive weight of slow, embodied craft.

c.headline: The Daily Heller: What is Portraiture in Digital Space?
c.summary: Steven Heller examines a body of work called Enter The Machine that expands portraiture to encompass digital entities such as files, folders, and programmes, raising urgent questions about identity, representation, and what it means to depict a subject in an age of algorithmic image-making. For visual communication students, it opens a productive critical space between traditional portraiture and the new ontology of machine-generated likenesses.
